title: Hidden surfaces, lighting and shading
subtitle: Decide which surface is in front, then decide how bright it looks.

hsr.title: Visible-surface determination
hsr.body: When objects overlap, only the nearest surface along each line of sight may be drawn. Object-space methods compare polygons geometrically (painter’s algorithm); image-space methods decide per pixel. Back-face detection discards polygons facing away: a face is hidden if its normal N and the view vector V satisfy N·V > 0 (roughly half the faces of a closed solid).
hsr.steps: A face has normal N = (0, 0, −1); the viewer looks along V = (0, 0, −1) (into the screen). N·V = 1 > 0 means the face points away from the viewer: back-facing, cull it.

z.title: The Z-buffer
z.body: The Z-buffer keeps, for every pixel, the depth of the nearest surface drawn so far. Start with depth = ∞. For each polygon and each pixel it covers, compute the depth z; if z is smaller (nearer) than the stored value, write the colour and the new depth. Polygons can arrive in any order — no sorting, simple in hardware, cost O(pixels × overlapping surfaces) and one depth value per pixel. The A-buffer adds transparency; scan-line methods handle one row at a time.

light.title: Illumination models
light.body: The Phong model sums three terms: ambient I = kₐ (light from everywhere), diffuse kd·cos θ (Lambert: proportional to the angle between the normal and the light — matte surfaces) and specular ks·cosⁿ α (a highlight where the reflection points at the eye; larger n = tighter, shinier). With ka = 0.1, kd = 0.5, ks = 0.4, n = 10, a surface lit head-on has I = 1; at 60° it drops to 0.35.

shade.title: Shading methods
shade.body: Computing the illumination model at every pixel is expensive, so surfaces are shaded by interpolation. Constant (flat) shading: one intensity per polygon — faceted look. Gouraud: compute intensity at the vertices and interpolate across the polygon — smooth, but can miss highlights that fall inside a polygon. Phong shading: interpolate the normals and apply the illumination model per pixel — accurate highlights, more expensive.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Back-face: N·V > 0 → cull. Z-buffer: keep the nearest fragment per pixel.
  • Phong model = ambient + diffuse + specular; flat < Gouraud < Phong shading.
